scope: Numbers 5–6, all 58 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 5–6. All 58 exact original records are hashed, with no note elements in this scope. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains the divine speaker and Moses as the recipient of the camp instructions.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves all three excluded groups; avoids equating tsaraat with a single modern diagnosis and retains corpse-related uncleanness.
verses.before: “Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone with a skin disease, everyone with a bodily discharge, and everyone made unclean by contact with a dead body.
verses.after: “Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone with a defiling skin condition, everyone with a bodily discharge, and everyone made unclean by a dead person.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone with a skin disease, everyone with a bodily discharge, and everyone made unclean by contact with a dead body.

verses.rationale: Keeps both sexes, repeated expulsion, the plural camps and divine dwelling as the stated reason; does not recast exclusion as voluntary.
verses.before: You will send out both male and female; send them outside the camp so that they do not defile their camps, in whose midst I dwell.”
verses.after: Send them out, male and female alike. Send them outside the camp so that they do not make their camps unclean, for I dwell among them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall send out both male and female; send them outside the camp so that they do not defile their camps, in whose midst I dwell.”

verses.rationale: Retains both the actual removal and the repeated obedience summary.
verses.before: The Israelites did so and sent them outside the camp. As the LORD spoke to Moses, so the Israelites did.
verses.after: The Israelites did this and sent them outside the camp. They did just as the LORD had told Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites did so and sent them outside the camp. As the LORD spoke to Moses, so the Israelites did.

verses.rationale: Keeps the separate speech introducing restitution.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit inclusion of men and women, the general human-sin wording and breach of faith with the LORD; notes the alternative against-others reading.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites: When a man or woman commits any of the sins by which people act unfaithfully against the LORD, and that person becomes guilty,
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When a man or woman commits any of the sins people commit, breaking faith with the LORD, that person incurs guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites: When a man or woman commits any of the sins by which people act unfaithfully against the LORD, and that person becomes guilty,

verses.rationale: Uses singular they for the man-or-woman referent and preserves confession, principal, added fifth and recipient.
verses.before: they will confess the sin they have committed. They will make full restitution for the wrong, add one-fifth to it, and give it to the one they wronged.
verses.after: They must confess the sin they committed, make full restitution, add one-fifth to it, and give it to the person they wronged.
verses.tsw_comparator: they shall confess the sin they have committed. They shall make full restitution for the wrong, add one-fifth to it, and give it to the one they wronged.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the parties without adding death explicitly; retains the family redeemer, payment to the LORD for the priest and separate ram.
verses.before: But if the person has no close redeemer to whom restitution may be made, the restitution belongs to the LORD for the priest, in addition to the ram of atonement by which atonement is made for the guilty person.
verses.after: If the wronged person has no family redeemer to receive the restitution, it is to be paid to the LORD for the priest. This is in addition to the ram used to make atonement for the guilty person.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the person has no close redeemer to whom restitution may be made, the restitution belongs to the LORD for the priest, in addition to the ram of atonement by which atonement is made for the guilty person.

verses.rationale: Preserves the contribution category, sacred status and priest as recipient rather than declaring every offering wholly his.
verses.before: Every contribution from all the holy gifts the Israelites bring to the priest will belong to him.
verses.after: Every contribution from the Israelites’ holy gifts that they bring to the priest belongs to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every contribution from all the holy gifts the Israelites bring to the priest shall belong to him.

verses.rationale: Takes the first ownership pronoun as referring to the donor and makes the second recipient explicit; a note preserves the alternative priest referent.
verses.before: Each person’s holy gifts remain that person’s to give; whatever anyone gives to the priest belongs to the priest.”
verses.after: Each person’s holy gifts are their own; whatever they give to the priest belongs to the priest.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Each person’s holy gifts remain that person’s to give; whatever anyone gives to the priest belongs to the priest.”

verses.rationale: Retains the new speech before the jealousy procedure.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the sex-specific marriage relationship and conditional opening rather than treating every accused woman as already guilty.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If a man’s wife goes astray and acts unfaithfully against him,
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: If a man’s wife goes astray and breaks faith with him,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If a man’s wife goes astray and acts unfaithfully against him,

verses.rationale: Makes sexual intercourse explicit, retains secrecy, absence of witnesses and not-being-caught, without adding an established verdict.
verses.before: and a man lies with her sexually, but it is hidden from her husband and she has kept herself concealed, though she has defiled herself, and there is no witness against her and she was not caught;
verses.after: and another man has sexual intercourse with her without her husband knowing, so that her defilement remains hidden, with no witness against her and without her being caught,
verses.tsw_comparator: and a man lies with her sexually, but it is hidden from her husband and she has kept herself concealed, though she has defiled herself, and there is no witness against her and she was not caught;

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated jealousy language and both guilty and innocent possibilities before the procedure follows.
verses.before: and if a spirit of jealousy comes over her husband and he becomes jealous of his wife when she has defiled herself, or if a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife though she has not defiled herself,
verses.after: and a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife when she has defiled herself—or a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of her when she has not defiled herself—
verses.tsw_comparator: and if a spirit of jealousy comes over her husband and he becomes jealous of his wife when she has defiled herself, or if a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife though she has not defiled herself,

verses.rationale: Keeps husband as actor, barley amount, both prohibited additives and the jealousy/remembrance/guilt relationship.
verses.before: then the man will bring his wife to the priest. He will bring as her offering one-tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He will pour no oil on it and put no frankincense on it, for it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, bringing guilt to remembrance.
verses.after: then the husband is to bring his wife to the priest and bring an offering for her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He must not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, an offering of remembrance that brings guilt to mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the man shall bring his wife to the priest. He shall bring as her offering one-tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall pour no oil on it and put no frankincense on it, for it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, bringing guilt to remembrance.

verses.rationale: Preserves priestly agency and the woman’s placement without describing the act as her voluntary choice.
verses.before: The priest will bring her near and have her stand before the LORD.
verses.after: The priest is to bring her forward and have her stand before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall bring her near and have her stand before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains holy water, clay and sanctuary-floor dust without adding a water source or chemical explanation.
verses.before: The priest will take holy water in an earthen vessel, and the priest will take some dust from the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.
verses.after: He is to take holy water in a clay vessel, take some dust from the tabernacle floor, and put it into the water.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel, and the priest shall take some dust from the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated standing, action on her hair, distinct items in her hands and his, and bitter curse-bearing water; notes uncovering as an alternative.
verses.before: The priest will have the woman stand before the LORD, loosen the woman’s hair, and place in her hands the grain offering of remembrance, which is the grain offering of jealousy. In the priest’s hand will be the bitter water that brings a curse.
verses.after: The priest is to have the woman stand before the LORD, loosen her hair, and place the offering of remembrance—the grain offering for jealousy—in her hands. He is to hold the bitter water that brings a curse.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall have the woman stand before the LORD, loosen the woman’s hair, and place in her hands the grain offering of remembrance, which is the grain offering of jealousy. In the priest’s hand shall be the bitter water that brings a curse.

verses.rationale: Retains the oath, innocence condition and under-husband expression, with harm exemption rather than an assumption of guilt.
verses.before: Then the priest will put her under oath and say to the woman, ‘If no man has lain with you, and if you have not turned aside to impurity while under your husband, be free from this bitter water that brings a curse.
verses.after: The priest is to put her under oath and say, ‘If no other man has slept with you, and you have not gone astray into defilement while under your husband’s authority, may you be unharmed by this bitter water that brings a curse.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the priest shall put her under oath and say to the woman, ‘If no man has lain with you, and if you have not turned aside to impurity while under your husband, be free from this bitter water that brings a curse.

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrasting condition and interrupted speech without inventing its completion before the priest’s curse formula.
verses.before: But if you have turned aside while under your husband, if you have defiled yourself and a man other than your husband has had sexual relations with you’—
verses.after: But if you have gone astray while under your husband’s authority, if you have defiled yourself and a man other than your husband has had sexual intercourse with you—’
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you have turned aside while under your husband, if you have defiled yourself and a man other than your husband has had sexual relations with you’—

verses.rationale: Retains oath and curse, divine agency and bodily images without silently choosing miscarriage or infertility as a precise diagnosis.
verses.before: then the priest will put the woman under the oath of the curse and say to her—‘may the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people when the LORD causes your thigh to fall and your abdomen to swell.
verses.after: The priest is to put the woman under this oath of cursing and say to her, ‘May the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the LORD makes your thigh waste away and your belly swell.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the priest shall put the woman under the oath of the curse and say to her—‘may the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people when the LORD causes your thigh to fall and your abdomen to swell.

verses.rationale: Keeps the body effects in their reversed order, curse-bearing water and the woman’s doubled response.
verses.before: May this water that brings a curse enter your body, causing your abdomen to swell and your thigh to fall.’ And the woman will say, ‘Amen, amen.’
verses.after: May this water that brings a curse enter your body, making your belly swell and your thigh waste away.’ Then the woman is to say, ‘Amen, amen.’
verses.tsw_comparator: May this water that brings a curse enter your body, causing your abdomen to swell and your thigh to fall.’ And the woman shall say, ‘Amen, amen.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the written curses and their removal into the water without adding a specific ink composition.
verses.before: The priest will write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
verses.after: The priest is to write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.

verses.rationale: Keeps coercive priestly agency, repeated curse/water language and bitterness; notes the later resumption of drinking in verses 26–27.
verses.before: Then he will make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and the water that brings a curse will enter her for bitterness.
verses.after: He is to make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and the curse-bearing water will enter her with bitter effects.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he shall make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and the water that brings a curse shall enter her for bitterness.

verses.rationale: Retains the transfer from her hands and separate waving and altar presentation.
verses.before: The priest will take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman’s hand, elevate the grain offering before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
verses.after: The priest is to take the grain offering for jealousy from the woman’s hands, wave it before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman’s hand, elevate the grain offering before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps the handful, memorial portion, burning and explicit after-that sequence without omitting repeated drinking language.
verses.before: The priest will take a handful of the grain offering as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar; afterward he will make the woman drink the water.
verses.after: He is to take a handful of the grain offering as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar. After that he is to make the woman drink the water.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall take a handful of the grain offering as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar; afterward he shall make the woman drink the water.

verses.rationale: Retains the conditional guilt, actual threatened bodily harm and public curse without giving a medical mechanism or assuming pregnancy.
verses.before: When he has made her drink the water, if she has defiled herself and acted unfaithfully against her husband, the water that brings a curse will enter her for bitterness; her abdomen will swell and her thigh will fall, and the woman will become a curse among her people.
verses.after: When he makes her drink the water, if she has defiled herself and broken faith with her husband, the curse-bearing water will enter her with bitter effects. Her belly will swell, her thigh will waste away, and she will become a curse among her people.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he has made her drink the water, if she has defiled herself and acted unfaithfully against her husband, the water that brings a curse will enter her for bitterness; her abdomen will swell and her thigh will fall, and the woman will become a curse among her people.

verses.rationale: Preserves the innocent alternative and seed-related fertility outcome, with the literal expression explained in a note.
verses.before: But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be free and will be able to conceive children.
verses.after: But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be unharmed and able to conceive.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she shall be free and shall be able to conceive children.

verses.rationale: Keeps the summary as a continuation into verse 30 and retains the sex-specific relationship and defilement condition.
verses.before: This is the instruction concerning jealousy, when a wife under her husband goes astray and defiles herself,
verses.after: This is the instruction for jealousy: when a wife goes astray while under her husband’s authority and defiles herself,
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the instruction concerning jealousy, when a wife under her husband goes astray and defiles herself,

verses.rationale: Retains the alternative suspicion case, husband’s presentation and priest’s full procedure; does not merge suspicion into established wrongdoing.
verses.before: or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he becomes jealous of his wife. He will have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest will carry out for her all this instruction.
verses.after: or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he becomes jealous of his wife. He is to have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest is to carry out this entire instruction for her.
verses.tsw_comparator: or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he becomes jealous of his wife. He shall have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest shall carry out for her all this instruction.

verses.rationale: Preserves the asymmetrical closing statement and bear-guilt idiom; does not add a punishment for the husband or erase the innocent outcome in verse 28.
verses.before: The man will be free from guilt, but the woman will bear her guilt.”
verses.after: The husband will be free from guilt, but the woman will bear her guilt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The man shall be free from guilt, but the woman shall bear her guilt.”

verses.rationale: Retains the new speech boundary for Nazirite instructions.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:

verses.rationale: Preserves both sexes and the special vow, connects Nazirite with separation, and uses inclusive pronouns for the explicitly mixed referent.
verses.before: Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When a woman or a man makes a special vow—the vow of a Nazirite—to set themselves apart for the LORD,
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: If a man or woman makes a special vow, a Nazirite vow, to set themselves apart for the LORD,
verses.tsw_comparator: Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When a woman or a man makes a special vow—the vow of a Nazirite—to set themselves apart for the LORD,

verses.rationale: Preserves wine, shekhar, both vinegars, the uncertain grape-soaking drink and fresh/dried grapes rather than reducing the rule to alcohol alone.
verses.before: they will abstain from wine and strong drink; they will drink neither wine vinegar nor strong drink vinegar, and will not drink any grape juice or eat fresh or dried grapes.
verses.after: that person must abstain from wine and other strong drink. They must not drink vinegar made from either, or any drink made by soaking grapes, and they must not eat fresh or dried grapes.
verses.tsw_comparator: they shall abstain from wine and strong drink; they shall drink neither wine vinegar nor strong drink vinegar, and shall not drink any grape juice or eat fresh or dried grapes.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated duration and comprehensive seeds-to-skins restriction.
verses.before: All the days of their separation they will not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, from the seeds to the skin.
verses.after: Throughout their time of separation, they must eat nothing that comes from the grapevine, from the seeds to the skins.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the days of their separation they shall not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, from the seeds to the skin.

verses.rationale: Keeps the razor image, duration, holiness and uncut hair without making the vow male-only.
verses.before: All the days of the vow of their separation, no razor will pass over their head; until the time is completed for which they have set themselves apart for the LORD, they will be holy, letting the hair of their head grow freely.
verses.after: Throughout the vow of separation, no razor is to pass over their head. Until the time they have set apart for the LORD is complete, they are to be holy and let the hair of their head grow freely.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the days of the vow of their separation, no razor shall pass over their head; until the time is completed for which they have set themselves apart for the LORD, they shall be holy, letting the hair of their head grow freely.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated duration and prohibition on approach to a human corpse.
verses.before: All the days that they are set apart for the LORD, they will not go near a dead body.
verses.after: Throughout their separation to the LORD, they must not go near a dead person.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the days that they are set apart for the LORD, they shall not go near a dead body.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four close relationships and the costly restriction, preserving the head/consecration image for explanation in the note.
verses.before: Even for father or mother, for brother or sister, they will not make themselves unclean when they die, because the separation to God is upon their head.
verses.after: They must not make themselves unclean when their father, mother, brother or sister dies, because their consecration to God is on their head.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even for father or mother, for brother or sister, they shall not make themselves unclean when they die, because the separation to God is upon their head.

verses.rationale: Retains the brief repeated holiness declaration rather than omitting it as redundant.
verses.before: All the days of their separation, they are holy to the LORD.
verses.after: Throughout their separation, they are holy to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the days of their separation, they are holy to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the doubled suddenness, involuntary defilement, consecrated head and repeated shaving instruction with the exact day.
verses.before: If someone dies suddenly beside them, defiling the head of their separation, they will shave their head on the day of their cleansing; on the seventh day they will shave it.
verses.after: If someone suddenly dies beside them, unexpectedly, and defiles their consecrated head, they are to shave their head on the day of their cleansing. They must shave it on the seventh day.
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone dies suddenly beside them, defiling the head of their separation, they shall shave their head on the day of their cleansing; on the seventh day they shall shave it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the next day, alternative bird pairs, priest and entrance location.
verses.before: On the eighth day they will bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.after: On the eighth day they are to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the eighth day they shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

verses.rationale: Retains sin and atonement terminology in the involuntary corpse case, both distinct offerings and same-day reconsecration; does not assign an unstated final-clause agent.
verses.before: The priest will offer one as a purification offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for them, because they sinned by contact with the dead body. That same day they will consecrate their head again.
verses.after: The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, making atonement for the person’s sin in connection with the dead person. That same day their head is to be made holy again.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall offer one as a purification offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for them, because they sinned by contact with the dead body. That same day they shall consecrate their head again.

verses.rationale: Keeps restarting the full period, year-old male lamb, guilt offering and lost prior days with the stated reason.
verses.before: They will separate themselves to the LORD for the days of their separation, and bring a male lamb a year old as a guilt offering. The previous days will be void, because their separation was defiled.
verses.after: They must set apart their time of separation for the LORD again and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The earlier days will not count, because their separation was defiled.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall separate themselves to the LORD for the days of their separation, and bring a male lamb a year old as a guilt offering. The previous days shall be void, because their separation was defiled.

verses.rationale: Uses passive for the unspecified bringer, retaining completion and sanctuary entrance rather than silently changing the Hebrew to self-arrival.
verses.before: This is the law for the Nazirite: when the time of their separation has been completed, they will be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.after: This is the instruction for the Nazirite when the time of separation is complete: the person is to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the law for the Nazirite: when the time of their separation has been completed, they shall be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

verses.rationale: Preserves number, age, animal sex, freedom from defect and each distinct offering assignment.
verses.before: They will present their offering to the LORD: one male lamb a year old without blemish as a burnt offering, one ewe lamb a year old without blemish as a purification offering, and one ram without blemish as a well-being offering,
verses.after: They are to bring their offering to the LORD: one year-old male lamb without defect as a burnt offering, one year-old female lamb without defect as a sin offering, and one ram without defect as a peace offering,
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall present their offering to the LORD: one male lamb a year old without blemish as a burnt offering, one ewe lamb a year old without blemish as a purification offering, and one ram without blemish as a well-being offering,

verses.rationale: Keeps both bread preparations, fine flour, no leaven and the accompanying plural grain and drink offerings.
verses.before: along with a basket of unleavened bread—cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil—and their grain offering and their drink offerings.
verses.after: with a basket of unleavened bread made from fine flour—loaves mixed with oil and unleavened wafers spread with oil—along with the grain offerings and drink offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: along with a basket of unleavened bread—cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil—and their grain offering and their drink offerings.

verses.rationale: Makes the presented objects clear and retains sin-before-burnt order at performance, distinct from the earlier inventory order.
verses.before: The priest will present them before the LORD and offer their purification offering and their burnt offering,
verses.after: The priest is to present these before the LORD and offer the person’s sin offering and burnt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall present them before the LORD and offer their purification offering and their burnt offering,

verses.rationale: Preserves ram, sacrifice, bread basket and accompanying offerings, with priestly agency repeated as in the source.
verses.before: and will offer the ram as a well-being offering to the LORD, together with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest will also offer the grain offering and the drink offering.
verses.after: He is to offer the ram to the LORD as a peace-offering sacrifice, together with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest is also to present its grain offering and drink offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: and shall offer the ram as a well-being offering to the LORD, together with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest shall also offer the grain offering and the drink offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps location, the consecrated head, removed hair and fire beneath the sacrifice; does not put the hair on a different altar or discard it.
verses.before: Then the Nazirite will shave the head of their separation at the entrance of the tent of meeting, take the hair from the head of their separation, and put it on the fire that is under the sacrifice of well-being.
verses.after: At the entrance of the tent of meeting, the Nazirite is to shave their consecrated head. They are to take the hair from that head and put it on the fire beneath the peace-offering sacrifice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Nazirite shall shave the head of their separation at the entrance of the tent of meeting, take the hair from the head of their separation, and put it on the fire that is under the sacrifice of well-being.

verses.rationale: Leads with the source’s timing clause, retaining the cooked portion, individual bread counts and hands as the receiving location.
verses.before: The priest will take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and place them in the hands of the Nazirite after the hair of their separation has been shaved.
verses.after: After the Nazirite has shaved their consecrated head, the priest is to take the ram’s boiled shoulder, one unleavened loaf from the basket and one unleavened wafer, and place them in the Nazirite’s hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and place them in the hands of the Nazirite after the hair of their separation has been shaved.

verses.rationale: Preserves presentation, priest’s extra portions and the explicit permission to resume wine only afterward, using the earlier Leviticus terms.
verses.before: The priest will elevate them as an offering before the LORD. They are holy for the priest, together with the breast that is elevated and the thigh that is raised. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.
verses.after: The priest is to wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. They are holy and belong to the priest, in addition to the breast of the wave offering and the contributed thigh. After this, the Nazirite may drink wine.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall elevate them as an offering before the LORD. They are holy for the priest, together with the breast that is elevated and the thigh that is raised. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.

verses.rationale: Keeps vowed offering, additional means and fulfillment of the actual vow without reducing the obligation to a suggested contribution.
verses.before: This is the law of the Nazirite who makes a vow—of their offering to the LORD for their separation—apart from what else their means may afford. According to the vow that they make, so they will do, in keeping with the law of their separation.
verses.after: This is the instruction for the Nazirite who vows an offering to the LORD for their separation, besides anything else they can afford. They must do what they vowed, in keeping with the instruction for their separation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the law of the Nazirite who makes a vow—of their offering to the LORD for their separation—apart from what else their means may afford. According to the vow that they make, so they shall do, in keeping with the law of their separation.

verses.rationale: Retains the separate divine speech introducing the blessing.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:

verses.rationale: Keeps Aaron and his sons as speakers commissioned to bless Israel and leads directly into the poetic words.
verses.before: Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: Thus you will bless the Israelites; you will say to them:
verses.after: “Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
verses.tsw_comparator: Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: Thus you shall bless the Israelites; you shall say to them:

verses.rationale: Retains the familiar source-faithful blessing and guarding pair, with explicit wish force and no change merely to reduce overlap.
verses.before: The LORD bless you and keep you;
verses.after: ‘May the LORD bless you and keep you;
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD bless you and keep you;

verses.rationale: Preserves the divine face and shining image, grace and second invocation of the LORD; lineation follows the two clauses.
verses.before: the LORD make the LORD’s face shine upon you and be gracious to you;
verses.after: may the LORD make his face shine on you and be gracious to you;
verses.tsw_comparator: the LORD make the LORD’s face shine upon you and be gracious to you;

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated face image and lifting rather than replacing it with an explanation, ending in shalom with its breadth noted.
verses.before: the LORD lift up the LORD’s face toward you and give you peace.
verses.after: may the LORD lift his face toward you and give you peace.’
verses.tsw_comparator: the LORD lift up the LORD’s face toward you and give you peace.

verses.rationale: Preserves the name-placement image, priestly plural they and emphatic divine I rather than attributing blessing solely to the priests.
verses.before: So they will put my name upon the Israelites, and I will bless them.
verses.after: So they will place my name on the Israelites, and I myself will bless them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So they shall put my name upon the Israelites, and I will bless them.
